articles.title: Kid IQ
articles.contents:
Kid IQ




By: Akmal G Date: November 4th, 2025
For one of my first works while learning from the University of
Essex, I created a visualization that shows how a mother’s education, IQ
and work status combined to influence childrens’ test scores. The
visualization revealed a number of patterns of advantages and
disadvantages across different family backgrounds.
The kidiq data stems from the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth
and is used in Gelman and Hill (2007). The data set contains 434
observations measured on five variables, and is obtained from https:
//github.com/jknowles/BDAexampleR.data
I used the packages tidyverse, stringr, readr, ggplot2 and curl.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(stringr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(curl)
## Using libcurl 8.14.1 with LibreSSL/3.3.6
## 
## Attaching package: 'curl'
## The following object is masked from 'package:readr':
## 
##     parse_date
My approach was to create categories that combine mother’s education
and work status. Then, I processed child outcomes vary across these
combined categories.
# Download and mutate data
kidiq.raw <- read_csv("kidiq-2.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
kidiq <- kidiq.raw %>%
mutate(
  
# Create work status labels
work_status = case_when(
mom_work == 1 ~ "Not working",
mom_work == 2 ~ "Part-time",
mom_work == 3 ~ "Full-time",
mom_work == 4 ~ "Full-time+"
),
# Create highschool diploma success groups
highschool_diploma = case_when(
mom_hs == 0 ~ "High School Diploma",
mom_hs == 1 ~ "No High School Diploma",
),
# Create combined advantage categories
family_advantage = case_when(
mom_hs == 0 & mom_work <= 2 ~ "Low",
mom_hs == 0 & mom_work > 2 ~ "Mixed",
mom_hs == 1 & mom_work <= 2 ~ "Mixed",
mom_hs == 1 & mom_work > 2 ~ "High",
),
# Create age groups
age_group = case_when(
mom_age >= 17 & mom_age <= 20 ~ "Ages 17-20",
mom_age >= 21 & mom_age <= 23 ~ "Ages 21-23",
mom_age >= 24 & mom_age <= 26 ~ "Ages 24-26",
mom_age >= 27 & mom_age <= 29 ~ "Ages 27-29"
),
# Create IQ terciles for grouping
iq_group = case_when(
mom_iq <= quantile(mom_iq, 0.33, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Lower IQ",
mom_iq <= quantile(mom_iq, 0.67, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Middle IQ",
TRUE ~ "Higher IQ"
)
)

kidiq$age_group <- factor(kidiq$age_group, labels = c(
"Ages 17-20","Ages 21-23", "Ages 24-26","Ages 27-29"))
kidiq$iq_group <- factor(kidiq$iq_group, labels = c(
"Lower IQ", "Middle IQ", "Higher IQ"))
kidiq$work_status <- factor(kidiq$work_status, labels = c(
"Not working", "Part-time", "Full-time","Full-time+"))
kidiq$family_advantage <- factor(kidiq$family_advantage, labels = c(
"Low", "Mixed", "High"))
kidiq <- as.data.frame(kidiq)
To indicate different effects on IQ, I added additional dimensions
using different colors, size, and faceting to differentiate. In the end,
I was able to tell a story about social mobility and opportunity through
a readable violin plot.
k1 <- ggplot(kidiq, aes(x = family_advantage, y = kid_score, color = age_group)) +
geom_violin() +
facet_wrap(~age_group) +
scale_color_brewer(palette = "RdPu") +
labs(
title = "Family Ties? Does a mother’s educational and employment
background affect their child's performance",
subtitle = "Correlation between family advantage with child's",
x = "Mother's Household Advantage",
y = "Child's Test Score",
caption = "Data: Test scores and mother's characteristics") +
theme_minimal()
print(k1)

The correlation between a mother’s educational and employment
background, collectively known as Family Advantage, and the academic
performance of their children is shown across several age groups. Most
data seems to be sporadic,with notable exceptions being unemployed and
full-time working mothers in the age range 24-26, and unemployed mothers
in their late teens, having children who reached the mode performance
scores.
